chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥannān ibn Sadīr, who said:

I heard a man ask Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he said: “Sometimes I urinate and cannot manage to use water, and that becomes difficult for me.” So he said: “When you urinate and wipe yourself, then wipe your private part with your saliva; then if you find something, say: this is from that.”
Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Saʿdān ibn Muslim, from ʿAbd al-Raḥīm, who said:

I wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام regarding a castrated man who urinates and encounters hardship because of that, and then sees wetness after wetness. He said: “He performs wudu (ablution) and sprinkles water once during the day.”
ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they continue to notice wetness after urination and have difficulty maintaining taharah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal guidance for one who experiences difficulty with lingering wetness after urination. It instructs practical measures to remove hardship and establish a basis for disregarding doubtful moisture in the context of taharah and wudu (ablution).
